sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the appellant/s-claimant/s NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4722/2006 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/09/2024 undefined under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`MV Act' for short),

being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 15.3.2005 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gandhinagar in MACP Nos.670 of 1991, whereby the claim petition of the claimants was partly allowed by awarding compensation of Rs.3,07,800/- with 9% interest till date 31.12.2000 and with 6% interest and expenses thereafter, from the opponent nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally.

Though the total awarded amount was of Rs.5,13,000/-, deducting 40% of the amount towards the negligence attributed to the deceased, the learned Tribunal passed the award of Rs.3,07,800/-.
2.

The brief facts leading to filing of this appeals are such that it is stated in the complaint produced at Exh.34 before the learned Tribunal that on 5.4.91 at about 12.00 hours, as one Dr.Pashabhai Patel of Hasanpur village i.e. the complainant's-Kantilal Bhagwanbhai Patel's village was hurt on his head and as the complainant was relative of the said doctor, he took him for necessary treatment to Visnagar civil hospital and from there, for further treatment, he was to be shifted to Ahmedabad civil hospital in the ambulance matador vehicle no.GBL.9190 of the ownership of the hospital and this matador was being diven by driver Baldevji Rathod; that from Visnagar towards Ahmedabad,
when he was passing NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4722/2006 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/09/2024 undefined through Dholakuva at about 2.30 hours, one jeep bearing registration no.GJ.2.9885 came from opposite direction and going towards Gandhinagar and dashed with the driver side of the matador due to which the accident occurred and as both the vehicles were dashed on driver's side,
the passengers sitting therein were injured and they were taken to Gandhinagar civil hospital for necessary treatment.
The drivers of both the vehicles died during the treatment.
Therefore, the claimants filed various claim petitions, out of which, the claim petition no.670 of 1991 is filed by the claimants of deceased driver of ambulance-matador, for compensation.
3. Notices were issued, the issues were framed by the Tribunal.
Oral as well as documentary evidence were led before the Tribunal.
After hearing the submissions made by the rival parties, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition(s) and awarded compensation as noted above.
4. Heard learned advocates for the parties.
5. Learned advocate for the appellant/s-claimant/s has mainly assailed the impugned judgment and award on the ground of negligence.
He submitted that the learned Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation of Rs.5,13,000/- but NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4722/2006 JUDGMENT

DATED:
11/09/2024 undefined erred in holding the contributory negligence of the driver of the ambulance-matador to the extent of 40%, which can be seen from the panchanama and that the driver of ambulance who was going on the road with a patient in the ambulance to save him, has lost his own life due to the negligence of the jeep driver and therefore the learned Tribunal has erred in Foolba Baldevji Rathod vs Sushil Papers Idustries on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10272740/
2 holding the contributory negligence of the driver of the ambulance, that too at 40%.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submitted that as there is no negligency on the part of the deceased, then the compensation is to be paid to the claimants in total by the respondent no.4-insurance company with which the ambulance is insured.
He, therefore, submitted that the appeal deserves to be allowed by modifying the impugned judgment and award.

5.1 He also submitted that the insurance company with which the ambulance is insured cannot be exonerated from payment of liability and the claimants should get the compensation from the insurance company as the deceased was driver in the ambulance and he was a paid driver in the said ambulance.

Or else, if the policy does not cover the risk of driver, then the owner should be held liable to satisfy the award as the deceased was a paid driver in the ambulance and he was driving the said ambulance as employee of the employer-owner.

He relied on the judgments NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4722/2006 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/09/2024 undefined in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. V/s Prembai Patel and Others, reported in 2005 ACJ 1323 and Valiben Laxmanbhai Thakore (Koli) and others V/s Kandla Dock Labour Board reported in 2021 ACJ 2262 and submitted that the appeal be allowed.

sentences.text:
6. As against this, learned advocate for respondent no.2-insurance company of the offending jeep has submitted that the learned Tribunal has discussed the evidence led before it, more particularly,
the deposition of the complainant who is the eye witness to the incident wherein he has stated that the accident happened in the middle of the road and both the vehicles were driving rashly and speedily.

He, therefore, submitted that the learned Tribunal has considered the same and other evidence and then came to the conclusion that the driver of the ambulance has also not take care to avoid the accident and apportioned the negligence to both the vehicles, however, the negligence of the ambulance should have been apportioned more.
He, therefore, prayed to dismiss this appeal or modify to the extent of more negligence to the driver of the ambulance.

6.2 Learned advocate for the respondent no.4-insurance company of the ambulance has submitted that the negligence of the jeep should have been apportioned more than the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4722/2006 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/09/2024 undefined ambulance as the ambulance was in the middle of the road and it was in speed and dashed with the jeep.
He submitted that the jeep cannot be apportioned with more negligence and liability and therefore prayed to dismiss the appeal.
7. I have considered the submissions made by learned advocates for the parties and also perused the documents on record including the impugned judgment and award.
8. The first point raised in this appeal is the point of negligence attributed to the ambulance driver by the learned Tribunal.

In this regard, looking to the manner in which the accident has occurred,
the documentary evidence cannot be taken as a base for the negligence aspect; further, the drivers of both the vehicles expired and therefore their deposition could not be recorded to prove the accident;

however, if the complaint filed by the complainant-who was an eye witness to the incident and who was travelling along with the ambulance driver is seen, it is stated therein that the jeep driver came on the wrong side and dashed with the ambulance; that both the vehicles were in full speed; that the Foolba Baldevji Rathod vs Sushil Papers Idustries on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10272740/
3 incident occurred in the middle of the road; it is obvious that the ambulance carrying patient will be in speed, however, there is nothing to show that the jeep driver took his jeep on the left side to give way to the ambulance and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4722/2006 JUDGMENT DATED:
11/09/2024

entities.text: Foolba Baldevji Rathod vs Sushil Papers Idustries
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: undefined

in such type of cases wherein ambulance or fire safety vehicles are involved,
it is expected from the private vehicles like jeep in this case to take care and keep the vehicle in the left side to give way to ambulance and avoid accidents.
However, the same is not done in this case.

At the same time, the ambulance driver could have driven his ambulance little bit on the left side,
then also, the accident could have been avoided.
Therefore, this Court finds it proper to attribute negligence to the jeep driver at 90% and ambulance driver at 10%.
8.1 The next contention is that the learned Tribunal has erred in not holding the owner and insurance company of the ambulance liable to make the payment.
In this regard, it is proved that the ambulance is owned by original opponent no.3 and insured with the original opponent no.4 and that the deceased was employed driver of the opponent no.3.

However, from the insurance policy produced on the record, it is seen that it is an `act liability policy' and no other risks are covered under the said policy and there is nothing on record to show that the insurance company has accepted the premium for covering any other risks of the ambulance.
Therefore, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the amount of compensation.

Therefore, the judgment of Valiben Laxmanbhai Thakore (Koli) (supra) will not be NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4722/2006 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/09/2024 undefined helpful in this case as, it is held that once the insurance company accepts the premium, then it becomes liable to pay the compensation.
In this case, the same is not coming on record that the insurance company has accepted any premium for covering the risks.
8.2 However, the case of Prembai Patel and Others (supra) will be helpful to the claimants.

It is held in paragraphs 16 and 17 as under:
"16.

The High Court, in the impugned judgment, had held that if the legal representatives of the deceased employee approach Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal for payment of compensation to them by moving a petition under section 166 of the Act, the liability of the insurance company is not limited to the extent provided under the Workmen's Compensation Act and on its basis directed the appellant insurance company to pay the entire amount of compensation to claimants.

As shown above,
the insurance policy taken by the owner contained a clause that it was a policy for `Act liability' only.
This being the nature of policy the liability of appellant would be restricted to that arising under Workmen's Compensation Act.
The judgment of the High Court, therefore, needs to be modified accordingly.

17. The judgment of the High Court insofar as it relates to NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4722/2006 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/09/2024 undefined quantum of compensation and interest, which is to be paid to the claimants (the respondent Nos.3 to 6 herein) is affirmed.
The liability of the appellant insurance company to satisfy the award would be restricted to that arising under the Workmen's Compensation Act.

The respondent Nos.1 and 2 (owners of the vehicle) would be Foolba Baldevji Rathod vs Sushil Papers Idustries on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10272740/
4 liable to satisfy the remaining portion of the award."

sentences.text:
8.3 In the case on hand, as the deceased driver of ambulance is held 10% negligent for the accident,
however, he being the employee of the owner-respondent no.4 and the policy is `Act liability Policy,
in view of the aforesaid decision, the respondent no.4-owner is liable to satisfy the award to the extent of 10%.
8.3 No contention is raised by either of the learned advocates on the point of quantum.
Hence, this Court is not discussing anything on this point as the learned Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation.

8.4 However, as the manifest object of the provisions of the MV Act is to ensure that the party, who suffers injuries due to the use of the motor vehicle, and may be able to get the damages for the injuries sustained/death, the claimants cannot suffer for the technicalities of whether the owner/insurance company should pay the amount.

As the vehicle is insured NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4722/2006 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/09/2024 undefined with the insurance company,
However, in view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in number of cases, the appellant-insurance company shall first pay the amount of compensation to the claimant/s and then it shall have the right to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle involved in the accident by resorting to appropriate remedies available under the law.
9. In view of the above discussion, this appeal is partly allowed.

The impugned judgment and award dated 15.3.2005 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gandhinagar in MACP Nos.670 of 1991 is modified to the extent that the driver of the jeep is negligent to the extent of 90% and the driver of the ambulance is negligent to the extent of 10%.
The amount awarded towards compensation by the learned Tribunal to the claimants is of Rs.5,13,000/-, which is not disturbed in this appeal.

The original opponent nos.1 and 2-owner and insurance company of the jeep is liable to satisfy the award to the extent of 90% and the original opponent no.3-owner of the ambulance is liable to satisfy the award to the extent of 10%.

However, the opponent no.4-insurance company of the ambulance shall first pay the compensation to the claimants and then it shall have the right to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4722/2006 JUDGMENT DATED: 11/09/2024 undefined involved in the accident by resorting to appropriate remedies available under the law.
10. The respective insurance companies shall deposit the amount within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the order.

Thereafter, the amount lying with the Tribunal and/or in the FDR,
pursuant to the order of this Court if any, along with the deposited amount by way of this appeal,
shall be disbursed to the claimant, along with accrued interest thereon if any, by account payee cheque, after proper verification and after following due procedure, within a period of six weeks from today.
11. Rest of the award remains unaltered.
Modified decree be drawn accordingly.
Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
